name: Bauhaus product
summary: The workshop objects of the Bauhaus: lamps, tea sets and chairs built from the sphere, the cylinder and the cone in nickel, chrome, opal glass and bent steel tube, as models for mass production.

philosophy.core_thesis: An everyday object is a model for the factory: its form comes from plain geometry, its material and its use, and ornament has no place on it.
design_principles: Build each body from a sphere, a cylinder, a cone or a cube; show the solid, not a style.
Make each part do one job, and let the eye read the job: a stem carries, a shade spreads light, a handle holds.
Use bent steel tube of 20 to 25 mm for the frame of a seat or a table, and leave it bare and chromed.
Use opal glass for a diffuser, and nickel or chrome for the metal parts.
Keep the surfaces smooth and free of ornament; a screw or a joint stays in view.
Keep colour to the colour of the material, with black, white and one primary colour at most.
Draw each object so that a factory can make it in series from standard parts.
anti_patterns: Applied ornament, a moulded leaf or a scroll
Revival forms that copy a past style
Hidden joints that pretend the object is one piece
Dark polished hardwood and carved legs
Brass with a warm, aged patina

form.geometry: The sphere, the hemisphere, the cylinder, the cone and the disc, joined on one vertical or horizontal axis.
form.silhouette: A clear outline of two or three solids: a disc base, a straight stem and a dome or a sphere on top.
form.edges: Sharp edges on metal discs and rims, with a radius of 0 to 2 mm; tube bends have a radius of 2 to 3 times the tube diameter.
form.proportion: A table lamp is about 36 cm high with a shade of 18 cm; a base disc is about equal to the shade diameter.
form.ornament: None. The only pattern is the repeat of standard parts, such as a row of tubes or a band of rivets.
rules: Each object has 2 to 4 primary solids.
Each metal tube is 20 to 25 mm in diameter.
A shade, a bowl or a vessel is a part of a sphere or a cylinder.
No surface carries a motif; 0% of the surface is ornament.
A colour other than black, white, grey or the metal covers less than 10% of the object.

materials.rule: Metal and glass make about 60% of the visible surface; wood and textile take the rest, in plain colours.

finish.gloss: 70–95 GU on metal, 5–15 GU on glass and wood
finish.patina: The style wants a new, clean surface; chrome and nickel stay bright, and a scratched object is out of character.

hardware.section: Tube 20–25 mm, rods and stems 8–12 mm
hardware.joints: Screwed or riveted joints in view; bent tube instead of a welded corner where possible.
hardware.handles: A straight bar or a ring of round section, or a disc knob of black Bakelite or wood.
hardware.switches_and_taps: A round rotary switch or a small pull cord; a cross-head or lever tap on a cylinder body.

palette.strategy: The colour of the material: chrome, nickel and white opal glass, with black and one primary colour as a small accent.

manufacture.scale: Workshop prototypes, then licensed series of a few thousand pieces from firms that made lamps and steel furniture.
manufacture.signs: Spun rings on a metal dome, the smooth bend of a tube, and screws and rivets left in view.

objects.form: round rotary on a round base
glass dome on a metal base
tubular steel club chair with straps
fruit bowl in wire or steel

positive: white and grey with one red accent
studio product photograph, soft even light

canonical_works.maker: Wilhelm Wagenfeld and Carl Jakob Jucker

emotion.target_response: Calm trust in a clear object: the viewer sees what each part does and how it was made.

use_cases: lighting and hardware for a modernist interior
a still life for a design museum shop
hardware schedules for a period flat
avoid_when: The room needs warm, soft and tactile objects.
The brief asks for ornament or a period revival.

modifiers.how: Swap chrome tube for bent birch and oak, opal glass for layered shades, and canvas for wool.
Keep the primary solids, but cover them in laminate pattern and saturated colour.
Keep the order, but use white and grey plastic, a fine grid and small radii.

ornament_level.note: A trace of ornament comes only from repeated parts, such as rivets.

era_blend.note: A reissue or a new object in the same geometry keeps the style.
